title: Asynchronous Communication Concepts
learningObjectives: Explain the key ideas and terminology of asynchronous communication concepts.
Recognize how the concept is used in real software communication.
Identify common mistakes or risks associated with this topic.
Apply the concept to a small, fictional API scenario.
Review a communication design and justify appropriate choices.

understand.concept: Asynchronous communication allows a caller to start an operation and continue or await completion without assuming an immediate result. Network calls, events, queues, and callbacks may complete later. Programs must account for pending states, ordering, cancellation, failures, and concurrency. Asynchronous does not necessarily mean parallel; the exact execution model depends on the runtime.
understand.whyItMatters: Network and service operations have variable duration, so asynchronous handling keeps applications responsive and makes completion explicit.
understand.analogy: Think of a delivery process with a sender, a message, and a receiver who returns a confirmation or explanation.
understand.analogyLimit: Software communication may involve complex protocols, asynchronous timing, security, and partial failures that this everyday analogy cannot fully capture.

explain.narrative:
Asynchronous communication allows a caller to start an operation and continue or await completion without assuming an immediate result. Network calls, events, queues, and callbacks may complete later. Programs must account for pending states, ordering, cancellation, failures, and concurrency. Asynchronous does not necessarily mean parallel; the exact execution model depends on the runtime.

Use the protocol and service documentation as the authoritative guide for a real API. Examples here are conceptual and intentionally do not make live network calls.

commonMistakes: Assuming every request succeeds or returns the same shape.
Treating parsing as validation or authentication as authorization.
Ignoring timeout, rate-limit, and failure responses.
Embedding secret credentials in public client code.
Retrying operations without considering duplicate side effects.

independentTask.title: Independent Practice
independentTask.instructions: Design asynchronous handling for a search screen. Include loading, success, empty, error, cancellation, and multiple rapidly changing searches. Explain how stale responses are prevented from replacing newer results.
requirements: Use a fictional or toy service; do not include live secrets.
